answer: Graph-shaped attestation: each identity ties only to peers who independently attest in a local mesh, so a sybil must inherit the sparse graph structure rather than mint tokens. One link costs an attacker a small fee, but growing a large connected component forces repeated new attestations across fresh neighbors, making dense subgraphs costly to maintain. No single attestation proves worth; only slow mesh propagation limits takeover, while a comet of forged nodes leaves few valid paths and starves any reef of coherent support from the broader ocean.
